name: Safe means unpunishable
citation: library/mk2/arcade.frames.json: mileena/cLK/gap_px 61 -> on_hit -11, on_block -2, damage 6. mileena/HK/close/gap_px 61 -> on_hit -7, on_block -14, damage 16. reptile/HP/close/gap_px 62 -> FAF 8 (the fastest punisher), damage 24. reptile/HK -> damage 32 far / 16 close.
claim: One punisher, one program, two moves. Against Mileena's cLK (-2) Reptile's counter is thrown at his earliest actionable frame and she BLOCKS it -- 8 chip, not 32. Against her close HK (-14) the identical counter lands 16 on her while she holds Block from 13 frames earlier. punishable <=> advantage <= -(punisher's first_active_frame).

beats.name: safe-move-blocked
beats.note: cLK with a 10-frame crouch lead-in (kit.MoveSpec: down+button on the same frame enters something that contacts nothing). Contact f20, 2 chip.

beats.name: fastest-punish-fails
beats.note: Reptile drops guard at contact+1 and attacks at global f37 -- his earliest actionable frame, measured. Mileena is actionable at f39 and guards from there; his f45 contact registers 8 (chip), not 32. Classified by the damage register, never by zero-damage: a blocked MK2 hit still chips.

beats.name: reset-to-point-blank
beats.note: Staging, not a claim: cLK's +32 px of blocked pushback has to be walked back off before the same rung's close HK exists again. Reptile re-guards at local f22.

beats.name: unsafe-move-blocked
beats.note: gap 63 px -> this is CLOSE HK (4 chip / 16 on hit), not the far HK of sequence 2. She re-guards at local f13 -- as early as the input allows.

beats.name: the-punish-lands
beats.note: Identical counter, identical guard-release discipline, thrown at his earliest actionable frame (press+28). 16 damage through her held Block: her guard has not returned. -14 <= -8, so it is punishable; -2 was not.

notes: Reptile's close HP (FAF 8, the brief's punisher) is measured here as contact at press+8 for 24 damage at gap 61 -- but after cLK's +32 px pushback the gap is 93 px, outside HP's 72 px connect range, so the far-reaching HK is the punisher both halves of the differential use. Running the SAME button in both halves is what keeps this a one-variable comparison.
